paras: Have you ever eaten so much that you could not eat any more? Food is wonderful, but our body needs more than tasty food. Today we read a funny story about a boy who wished only for food. We will also learn why water is so important, see what happens when sugar and sand go into water, describe people, join sentences and make a table mat.

Krishna loved food. He always wanted to eat different kinds of food and snacks. He was never tired of eating. Every day, at noon, he would sit under a banyan tree and eat his lunch. One day, as he was eating, an old man came. Krishna felt sorry for him and shared his food with him. The old man was so happy that as he was leaving, he said, “My child, you have been so kind. In return, you can wish for anything from this tree and it will be granted.” Krishna felt very happy.
He thought, I can ask for different types of food, and enjoy them forever. He sat there and closing his eyes said, “Oh tree, let me have different types of food. Nothing else.”
He heard a voice from the tree. “You don’t want anything else? Think it over.” Without thinking, Krishna said, “Nothing else”. First, he asked for laddoos. At once, a basket full of laddoos appeared.

He happily started eating it. After some time, he got bored. Then he thought of colourful fruits. Immediately, fruit in baskets appeared. He started eating them. There were grapes, mangoes, apples, bananas, jackfruit, melons, guavas, oranges and many more. Then he got bored eating only fruits. He asked for savouries. Immediately savouries like matri, samosas, kachori, potato chips and vada appeared in huge baskets. He happily started eating them.
As he was eating, he suddenly got hiccups. He wanted water. He looked around. There was food everywhere but no water!
He asked for water but the tree said, “You wanted only food not water.”
“So what if I don’t get water I will have sharbat, kheer and badam milk for my thirst,” thought Krishna. Soon, all these appeared in jugs.
Krishna drank them all but the hiccups did not stop. They became louder. He was now desperate for water.
He prayed to the tree, “May all this food disappear, and let me have water instead.”
“Are you sure?” the voice from the tree asked.
“Yes, I am sure. Now I know the importance of water. No other drink can replace water. Please give me just water.”
A jug of water appeared. Thirsty, Krishna drank as though he had never seen water. His hiccups stopped. He was no longer thirsty.
— Sudha Murty
New words: forever, immediately, appeared, savouries, hiccups, disappear, instead, replace, thirsty

items.q: The old man said Krishna could wish for anything from the tree. What do you think Krishna will do now?
items.a: Teacher note: Open-ended prediction. Accept any sensible answer. Children check their guess after reading.

items.q: Krishna asked the tree for food and nothing else. What do you think will happen now?
items.a: Teacher note: Open-ended prediction. Accept any sensible answer, for example, 'He will eat too much' or 'He will get thirsty'.

items.q: 1. What did Krishna enjoy?
items.a: Krishna enjoyed eating different kinds of food and snacks.

items.q: 2. Do you think the old man had magical powers? How do you know?
items.a: Yes. He gave Krishna a tree that could grant any wish, and everything Krishna asked for appeared at once. (Teacher note: Accept any answer with a sensible reason.)

items.q: 3. Why did the tree ask Krishna to ‘think over’ his wish?
items.a: Teacher note: The tree wanted Krishna to think carefully and perhaps wish for something more useful than only food. Accept similar answers in the child’s own words.

items.q: 4. Name some of the things that Krishna ate.
items.a: Laddoos; fruits like grapes, mangoes, apples, bananas, jackfruit, melons, guavas and oranges; savouries like matri, samosas, kachori, potato chips and vada. He also drank sharbat, kheer and badam milk.

items.q: 1. Have you experienced hiccups?
items.a: Teacher note: Open-ended speaking activity. Let children share their experience.

items.q: 2. What do you do when you get hiccups?
items.a: Teacher note: Answers will vary (for example, drink water slowly, hold the breath for a few seconds). Do not suggest anything that can scare a child.

items.q: 3. Do you think water is important? Why do you think so?
items.a: Teacher note: Yes. We need water to drink, to cook, to wash and for plants and animals to live. Accept answers in simple words.

items.q: 4. If you were in Krishna’s place, what would you wish for and why?
items.a: Teacher note: Open-ended. Accept any answer with a reason.

paras: Read the following sentences.
1. Krishna shared his food with the old man. He is kind.
2. Krishna wanted to eat everything. He is greedy.
3. The old man gave a special gift to Krishna. He is generous.
Choose a word from the box to describe the people below: brave, polite, selfish, lazy.

sections.heading: D. Krishna enjoyed the following items. Write them in the correct basket.
sections.note: Help box: banana, kheer, melon, guava, kachori, potato chips, laddoo, vada, jackfruit, samosa. Teacher note: Add a three-basket table image here with the headings Fruits, Sweets and Salty snacks.

items.q: Fruits
items.a: banana, melon, guava, jackfruit

items.q: Sweets
items.a: kheer, laddoo

items.q: Salty snacks
items.a: kachori, potato chips, vada, samosa

sections.heading: E. Words that describe people.
sections.note: Teacher note: Draw learners’ attention to the idea of ‘quality’ or ‘property’. Words like kind, greedy and generous tell us what a person is like. Let learners describe someone or something around them.

items.q: Krishna shared his food with the old man. Which word tells us what Krishna is like?
items.a: kind

items.q: Krishna wanted to eat everything. Which word tells us what Krishna is like?
items.a: greedy

items.q: The old man gave a special gift to Krishna. Which word tells us what the old man is like?
items.a: generous

items.q: Write one describing word for a friend, a teacher or a family member.
items.a: Teacher note: Answers will vary (for example, helpful, funny, cheerful, tall).

sections.heading: F. Choose a word from the box to describe the people.
sections.note: Help box: brave, polite, selfish, lazy.

items.q: 1. Pramod doesn’t share his toys with anyone. He is ____________.
items.a: selfish

items.q: 2. The woman saved the boy from the robber. She is ____________.
items.a: brave

items.q: 3. Advait is always lying in bed and doing nothing. He is ____________.
items.a: lazy

items.q: 4. Prerna always wishes everyone in the morning. She is ____________.
items.a: polite

sections.heading: G. Joining sentences with ‘and’ or ‘but’.
sections.note: Read: Sam is watching television. Pratham is watching television. Both are doing the same thing, so we join them: Sam and Pratham are watching television. Aman has a pen. Aman has a pencil. Aman has an eraser. These can be joined as: Aman has a pen, a pencil and an eraser. Sam works in the afternoon. Pratham works at night. These can be joined with ‘but’: Sam works in the afternoon but Pratham works at night. Now rewrite the following sentences using ‘and’ or ‘but’.

items.q: 1. I eat an apple. I eat an orange. I eat a peach. (and)
items.a: I eat an apple, an orange and a peach.

items.q: 2. I like to watch cartoons. My sister likes to watch movies. (but)
items.a: I like to watch cartoons but my sister likes to watch movies.

items.q: 3. Anita plays volleyball. Anju plays volleyball. (and)
items.a: Anita and Anju play volleyball.

items.q: 4. Dolma wants a new comic book. She has spent all her pocket money on sweets. (but)
items.a: Dolma wants a new comic book but she has spent all her pocket money on sweets.

items.q: 5. Rajesh wants to go to the park. He has not finished his homework. (but)
items.a: Rajesh wants to go to the park but he has not finished his homework.

sections.heading: H. Let us listen.
sections.note: Teacher note: Read each part of the story aloud. Ask children to listen carefully and tell the class what happened after that.

items.q: Krishna said, “Oh tree, let me have different types of food. Nothing else.” What happened after that?
items.a: The tree asked him to think it over. He said ‘Nothing else’, and the food he asked for appeared: laddoos, then fruits, then savouries.

items.q: As he was eating, he suddenly got hiccups. He wanted water. What happened after that?
items.a: There was no water, only food. The tree reminded him that he had wished only for food. He drank sharbat, kheer and badam milk, but the hiccups did not stop. Finally he wished for water.

sections.heading: I. Let us write. Complete the following story.
sections.note: Teacher note: Add a large cloud outline image here for children to write inside.

items.q: Vijaya is a young girl. She lives with her father, mother, grandmother and grandfather in a small village. Each day ______________________
items.a: Teacher note: Accept any story with 3 to 5 correct sentences. Sample: Each day she wakes up early. She helps her grandmother water the plants. Then she goes to school with her friends. In the evening, she plays with her grandfather.

sections.heading: J. Fun with Words.
sections.note: Teacher note: Add a word pyramid image here. Notice that the first letter of each word in a line is the same letter. Carrots / Cut Carrots / Chandu Cut Carrots. Apples / Ate Apples / Anu Ate Apples.

items.q: Carrots, Cut Carrots, Chandu Cut Carrots. The first letter of each word is ____________.
items.a: C

items.q: Apples, Ate Apples, Anu Ate Apples. The first letter of each word is ____________.
items.a: A

items.q: Write similar words using your name or any name of your choice. The first letter of each word is ____________.
items.a: Teacher note: Answers will vary. Sample: Tara / Took Tomatoes / Tara Took Tomatoes. The first letter is T.

sections.heading: K. Read the incomplete sentences. Discuss with your friends and complete them.

items.q: 1. Krishna shared his food with the old man because ______________________.
items.a: he felt sorry for the old man (he was kind).

items.q: 2. Krishna was happy because ______________________.
items.a: the tree could grant him any wish.

items.q: 3. After eating fruits, Krishna asked for savouries because ______________________.
items.a: he got bored eating only fruits.

items.q: 4. Krishna asked for water because ______________________.
items.a: he had hiccups and was thirsty, and he understood that no other drink can replace water.

paras: Krishna learnt the hard way that food alone is not enough. Let us become young scientists and find out more about water, food and what happens when different things are put into water. For these activities you will need a few clear glasses, water, a spoon, sugar, salt, sand, a jug and a bowl.

sections.heading: Biology Corner: Water and healthy food

items.q: Why does our body need water? Give two reasons.
items.a: Water helps us digest food, keeps our body cool, and keeps us healthy and active. (Teacher note: Accept other simple, correct reasons.)

items.q: Krishna ate only sweets, fruits and savouries. A healthy plate has different kinds of food. Name one food that gives us energy, one that helps us grow, and one that keeps us healthy.
items.a: Teacher note: Sample: energy - rice or roti; helps us grow - dal, milk or egg; keeps us healthy - fruits and vegetables. Accept other correct examples.

items.q: Kheer and badam milk are made with milk. Where does milk come from?
items.a: From animals like cows and buffaloes.

sections.heading: Chemistry Corner: Solid or liquid? Dissolve or not?
sections.note: Teacher note: Fill three glasses with the same amount of water. Add one spoon of sugar to the first, one spoon of salt to the second and one spoon of sand to the third. Stir each for one minute and let children observe. Only taste the sugar water if the glass and spoon are clean and you allow it. Never taste the sand water.

items.q: Write solid or liquid: laddoo, sharbat, samosa, badam milk.
items.a: laddoo - solid; sharbat - liquid; samosa - solid; badam milk - liquid. (Teacher note: kheer is a thick liquid. Let children discuss it.)

items.q: Which things disappeared in the water: sugar, salt or sand? Which stayed at the bottom?
items.a: Sugar and salt dissolved (they seem to disappear), and the sand stayed at the bottom. Children should write what they actually observe.

items.q: Why is sharbat sweet?
items.a: Because sugar dissolves in the water and makes it sweet.

sections.heading: Physics Corner: Which one keeps its shape?
sections.note: Teacher note: Pour the same amount of water into a glass, a jug and a bowl. Ask children to look at how the water looks in each one.

items.q: What shape does the water take in the glass, the jug and the bowl?
items.a: Water takes the shape of the container it is in. Children should describe what they see.

items.q: Does the amount of water change when it goes from one container to another?
items.a: No, only the shape changes. The amount stays the same.

items.q: Which keeps its own shape, a laddoo or sharbat?
items.a: A laddoo. Solids keep their shape, but liquids take the shape of the container.

items.q: 1 litre of water is 1000 ml. A jug has 1 litre of water. How many glasses of 250 ml can you fill from it?
items.a: 1000 divided by 250 = 4 glasses.

items.q: Krishna drank 3 glasses of 250 ml each. How many ml of water did he drink? How much is left in the 1-litre jug?
A basket has 12 laddoos. Krishna ate 5 of them. How many laddoos are left?
items.a: 12 - 5 = 7 laddoos.

items.q: Class survey: Ask each child to name their favourite snack. Make tally marks on the board. Which snack got the most votes?
items.a: Teacher note: Answers will vary with the class. Help children count the tally marks and, if time permits, draw a simple bar chart.

paras: Let us do: Let us make a table mat.
Materials needed: an A4 sheet of paper, pictures of various fruits and vegetables, bits and pieces of coloured papers, glue and a pencil or a sketch pen.
Steps: 1. On the A4 sheet, draw fruits or vegetables of your choice like an apple, a mango or a pear.
2. Take the sheet of red coloured paper. Make small bits by tearing it.
3. Stick the bits of paper on the apple picture you made.
4. Likewise, stick the yellow paper or the colour you like in the mango picture.
5. You can cover it with any plastic sheet available in your house.
6. Your table mat is ready!

sections.heading: L. Talk about your table mat.

items.q: What materials did you use to make your table mat?
items.a: Teacher note: An A4 sheet, coloured paper, glue and a pencil or sketch pen. Accept other materials the child used.

items.q: Why do we tear the paper into small bits instead of cutting one big piece?
items.a: Teacher note: Small bits fill the shape neatly and give a textured look. Accept any sensible answer.

items.q: Why do you think we cover the mat with a plastic sheet?
items.a: To keep it clean and dry, and to protect it from water and food. (Teacher note: Plastic does not soak up water.)

items.q: Mix red and yellow paint. Which colour do you get?
items.a: Orange. (Teacher note: Let children try with paint or crayons on paper.)

items.q: Name a fruit that is red, one that is yellow and one that is green.
items.a: Teacher note: Sample: apple (red), banana or mango (yellow), grapes or guava (green).

items.q: Fold your A4 sheet in half. How many equal parts do you get?
items.a: 2 equal parts (halves).

items.q: Fold it in half again and open it. How many equal parts do you get now? What do we call each part?
items.a: 4 equal parts. Each part is a quarter.

items.q: Colour 1 quarter of your mat red and 2 quarters yellow. How many quarters are left?
items.a: 4 - 3 = 1 quarter is left.
